title: The Scent of Iron and Salt
story:
The grass grew taller as the morning bled into afternoon, brushing against James's ankles with a dry, whispering hiss. James had never walked so far beneath an unshaded sky. James had never felt the midday heat press quite so flat and wide upon his shoulders. James had never known a silence so vast that it made his own heartbeat sound like a drum in a hollow log.

The metallic scent on the wind grew sharper, losing its ghost of distance and sharpening into something cold and deliberate. It was not the smell of bruised leaves or wet stone, but of crushed shale and something burned down to charcoal. He paused by a jagged outcrop of grey rock, peering down into the shallow valley below where the hillside finally leveled out into grey-green flats.

There, caught between the curve of a dry creek bed and a low ridge of wind-bent scrub, lay his first curiosity of the open world. It was a long, straight rib of dull grey material that was neither wood nor bone, half-buried in the soil like a sleeping spine. He reached out a hesitant paw, brushed its cool, unforgiving edge, and pulled back with a shiver.

He did not take it with him, though the temptation to carry a piece of the great mystery lingered in his thoughts. Instead, he simply stood very still, watching a strange grey hawk circle lazily above the depression in the earth. The valley sloped downward still, promising further answers just beyond the next fold of land.
location: a rocky depression on the lower hillside overlooking a grey-green valley
